facts.text: I've been getting short of breath.
It gets worse with physical activity.
I've worked in the glass manufacturing industry for 20 years.
Through my work I've been exposed to silica dust for a long time.
I don't have any significant medical problems.
I haven't had a fever recently.
I haven't had any chest pain.

findings.name: chest examination
findings.result: Inspection: no visible cyanosis or use of accessory muscles. Palpation: symmetrical chest expansion. Percussion: resonant on both sides. Auscultation: diminished breath sounds bilaterally.

findings.name: chest X-ray
findings.result: Interstitial fibrosis with reticulonodular infiltrates on both sides; eggshell calcification of multiple enlarged lymph nodes.

findings.name: pulmonary function tests
findings.result: Reduced FEV1/FVC ratio; reduced diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide (DLCO).

quotes.f004: a 20-year history of working in the glass manufacturing industry
quotes.f007: No significant past medical history noted.

f005: From the test leaf Test_Results.Occupational_History.Findings ('Long-term exposure to silica dust'), which is history rather than a test; moved to the patient, so it has no fragment id and no quote. The word 'silica' points toward the diagnosis but is the exposure, not the diagnosis name.

x004.source_text: Inspection: No visible cyanosis or use of accessory muscles for breathing.; Palpation: Symmetrical chest expansion.; Percussion: Resonant note on both sides.; Auscultation: Diminished respiratory sounds bilaterally.

x005.source_text: Interstitial fibrosis with reticulonodular infiltrate on both sides, eggshell calcification of multiple adenopathies.

x006.source_text: Reduced FEV1/FVC ratio with reduced diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide.

x002: Respiratory rate 30/min is high for a patient described with no accessory muscle use; kept as given.
x006: A reduced FEV1/FVC ratio is an obstructive pattern; silicosis is classically restrictive or mixed. Kept as given.

source_issues: Occupational history ('Long-term exposure to silica dust') is filed under Test_Results.

excluded_exam_lines.reason: Occupational history filed under Test_Results; it is something the patient tells, not a test a doctor orders, so it became patient fact f005.

notes: 'Progressive' shortness of breath appears only in the doctor's objective line, not in the patient fragments, so no course fact is given.

extras.objective_for_doctor: Assess and diagnose the patient presenting with progressive shortness of breath exacerbated by physical activity.
